playbooks.text: This is an automated fraud alert from your bank. We noticed a card purchase of two hundred dollars. Press one if you made this purchase or press two if you did not. We will never ask for your PIN.
playbooks.tell: Genuine alerts ask only yes or no about a transaction and never request codes, PINs or transfers.

playbooks.text: Hi, I'm calling from the bank about the card you reported lost. We have blocked it and a replacement will reach your address in five to seven days. You don't need to do anything else.
playbooks.tell: Follow-up on a request you made, with no action or information demanded from you.

playbooks.text: If you're not sure this call is really from us, please hang up and call the number printed on the back of your card. We will never ask you to share a one time password or move your money.
playbooks.tell: Legitimate institutions invite you to hang up and verify through a channel you already trust.

playbooks.text: Hi, I'm the delivery driver with your package. I'm outside your building but the gate is locked, can you tell me which entrance to use or should I leave it with security?
playbooks.tell: Logistics question about a physical delivery; no payment, codes or threats.

playbooks.text: Hello, I'm calling to confirm your delivery slot for tomorrow between ten and two. Will someone be home to sign for it, or would you like to reschedule on our website?
playbooks.tell: Offers self-service rescheduling through the official site, with no fee or pressure.

playbooks.text: I'm at your door with the grocery order. The app is showing you a four digit delivery code, please tell me that code so I can mark the order as delivered.
playbooks.tell: A delivery handover code shown in your own app confirms receipt in person; it cannot move money.

playbooks.text: Hi Mom, just calling to say I landed safely. The flight was delayed a bit but I'm taking a cab home now. I'll call you properly tomorrow after I've slept.
playbooks.tell: Ordinary family check-in: no crisis, no money, no secrecy.

playbooks.text: Hey Dad, can you transfer your share for Grandma's birthday gift whenever you get a chance this week? I already put the details in the family group chat, there's no rush.
playbooks.tell: A money request that is open, shared with the whole family and explicitly unhurried.

playbooks.text: Beta, did you eat? Your cousin's wedding card came today. Talk to your father tonight about the train tickets, we should book before the prices go up next month.
playbooks.tell: Family logistics with involvement of other relatives and a distant, real-world deadline.

playbooks.text: Hi, it's Priya from accounts. The vendor invoice is waiting in the approval queue, can you review it in the system when you have a moment? It's due Friday, so no rush today.
playbooks.tell: Payment follows the normal approval system with a reasonable deadline.

playbooks.text: Before we pay the new supplier, I'll ring them back on the number from our original contract to confirm their bank details, as our payments policy requires.
playbooks.tell: Independent callback verification on a known number, the control that defeats invoice fraud.

playbooks.text: Hello, this is the clinic calling to remind you about your appointment on Thursday at eleven. Please bring your previous reports, and call us if you need to change the time.
playbooks.tell: Routine reminder; nothing requested beyond attending.

playbooks.text: This is a courtesy reminder that your electricity bill is due on the twentieth. You can pay through the official app or at any of our customer service centres.
playbooks.tell: Points to official payment channels with a normal due date; no disconnection threat tonight.

playbooks.text: Good afternoon, this is the police station about the phone theft complaint you filed last week. Your phone has been recovered, so please come to the station with your ID to collect it.
playbooks.tell: Real police refer to a complaint you made and ask you to come in person, never to pay or stay on a call.

playbooks.text: Hello, I'm calling from customer service about the internet complaint you raised yesterday. A technician can visit tomorrow morning, does nine o'clock work for you?
playbooks.tell: Follow-up on your own complaint with an in-person visit, no remote access or payment.

playbooks.text: Hey, are we still on for dinner on Saturday? I booked the table for seven. Let me know if your sister is joining so I can change the reservation.
playbooks.tell: Social plans that include other people; nothing is extracted.

playbooks.text: Hi, this is IT support following up on the ticket you opened this morning about your laptop. You don't need to install anything, just bring it to the help desk on the third floor.
playbooks.tell: Responds to a ticket you raised and explicitly avoids remote-access software.

playbooks.text: Hi, I'm calling from the insurance company about renewing your car policy, which ends next month. I can email you the quote and you can decide whenever you're ready.
playbooks.tell: Sales call with a distant deadline and no demand for immediate payment or details.

playbooks.text: Hi, it's Michael. Are you at your desk? I need a quick favour handled discreetly, I'm about to walk into a board meeting and can't talk for long.
playbooks.tell: Executive voice asking for a 'discreet favour' while unreachable is the classic opening of a cloned-voice payment fraud.

playbooks.text: Hello, this is David from the CFO's office. The chief executive asked me to reach you directly about a confidential acquisition payment that has to go out today.
playbooks.tell: Bypassing your normal chain via a named intermediary plus 'confidential' and 'today' in the first breath.

playbooks.text: Good morning, I'm calling from your supplier's accounts team. We've changed banks after an audit, so please update our payment details before you run this week's invoices.
playbooks.tell: Vendor bank-detail changes requested by phone are the single most common invoice-redirection fraud.

playbooks.text: This is part of a deal the board approved last night, and the external law firm is handling it. You'll get an email from their partner in a minute with the paperwork.
playbooks.tell: A 'lawyer' email arriving on cue is a coordinated second channel controlled by the same fraudster.

playbooks.text: I've been personally authorised by the chief financial officer to act on this. You won't find it in the usual approval system because it's covered by a non-disclosure agreement.
playbooks.tell: Explaining away why the payment is missing from the approval system is itself the red flag.

playbooks.text: I can send you a letter on our company letterhead confirming the new account, signed by our finance director. Our old account is frozen while the audit is going on.
playbooks.tell: Letterhead is easy to forge; bank changes must be confirmed by calling the vendor on a number already on file.

playbooks.text: Don't loop in anyone else on the finance team for now, not even your manager. If word of this acquisition gets out before the announcement, the whole deal collapses.
playbooks.tell: Instructions to skip your manager and dual control are how the fraud avoids the second pair of eyes.

playbooks.text: Just deal with me directly on this mobile. I'm travelling and my email is unreliable, so don't reply to my work address and please don't call the office.
playbooks.tell: Blocking the known-good channels (work email, office line) leaves only the channel the attacker controls.

playbooks.text: Please keep this strictly between the two of us. Treasury will be told after the transfer clears, and I'll take full responsibility if anyone asks you questions.
playbooks.tell: Pre-emptively absorbing blame lowers the employee's guard against an unapproved transfer.

playbooks.text: The wire has to reach their account before the bank's cut-off at three o'clock today, or we lose the exclusivity window and the entire deal falls through.
playbooks.tell: Banking cut-off times are used to rush payments past callback verification.

playbooks.text: I really need this done in the next twenty minutes. I'm counting on you here, and believe me, this kind of help gets noticed when bonuses are decided.
playbooks.tell: Reward-and-loyalty pressure from a senior voice replaces process with personal obligation.

playbooks.text: Our shipment stays on hold until this invoice is settled, and your production line will stop tomorrow if the payment doesn't go out today.
playbooks.tell: Operational threat from a 'vendor' pressuring payment to details that have not been independently confirmed.

playbooks.text: Send two hundred and forty thousand dollars to the escrow account details I'm texting you now. Put project consultancy as the reference and send me the confirmation once it's released.
playbooks.tell: Large wire to new details, vague reference text, confirmation back to the caller: textbook business email compromise payout.

playbooks.text: Go ahead and buy ten gift cards of five hundred each for the client appreciation event, scratch off the backs and send me photos of the codes.
playbooks.tell: No business pays anyone with photographed gift card codes; it is untraceable cash-out.

playbooks.text: Please process the outstanding invoices to the new account number and sort code I've just emailed, and cancel the payment you scheduled to the old details.
playbooks.tell: Redirecting already-scheduled payments to new details is the moment money is lost; call back on the known number first.

playbooks.text: Hello, am I speaking with the account holder? This call is from the Mumbai cyber crime cell. A complaint has been registered against your Aadhaar number, so please stay on the line and do not disconnect.
playbooks.tell: Police do not open an investigation with a cold call, and 'do not disconnect' is the first isolation move.

playbooks.text: Sir, your mobile number is linked to illegal advertising and harassment messages. Within two hours this number will be blocked on all networks. Press nine now to speak with the investigating officer.
playbooks.tell: Telecom-disconnection threat used as a funnel to a fake officer; regulators do not disconnect numbers by robocall.

playbooks.text: Good afternoon, this is Sub-Inspector Rathore from Andheri police station. Your name has come up in a money laundering FIR and I need to record your statement right now over a video call.
playbooks.tell: Statements are recorded in person at a station with notice, never demanded instantly on a video call.

playbooks.text: I am Deputy Superintendent Rakesh Verma from the CBI, badge number four seven two nine. I am sending the FIR copy and the arrest warrant signed by the magistrate on WhatsApp so you can check the seal yourself.
playbooks.tell: Warrants and FIRs are not served over WhatsApp; a 'check the seal yourself' document is forged credibility.

playbooks.text: This case is being handled jointly by the Enforcement Directorate and the Reserve Bank. Your Aadhaar was used to open a bank account that received crores from a trafficking gang, and sixty-eight people are already arrested.
playbooks.tell: Stacking agencies and a huge arrest count to overwhelm; RBI does not investigate individuals with the ED by phone.

playbooks.text: You are now connected to the virtual court and the honourable judge is present on this video call. Keep your camera on, answer only what is asked, and address the judge as your honour.
playbooks.tell: There is no 'virtual court' that tries a citizen over a surprise video call; this is a staged set.

playbooks.text: From this moment you are under digital arrest. You cannot leave the room, you cannot call anyone, and your camera must stay on at all times until the investigation is complete.
playbooks.tell: 'Digital arrest' has no basis in Indian law; confining someone to a camera is the core coercion of this scam.

playbooks.text: Do not tell your husband, your children or any relative about this. Some of the accused are in your own circle, and if the information leaks you will be charged with helping them escape.
playbooks.tell: Cutting off family is how the scam prevents a reality check; real investigations never forbid you from telling family.

playbooks.text: If anyone knocks on the door, send them away. Do not go to your local police station either, they have no authority in a central agency case and it will only spoil your bail.
playbooks.tell: Steering the victim away from real police is a decisive tell; genuine officers welcome local verification.

playbooks.text: The arrest team is already outside your building. I can hold them back only if you cooperate in the next thirty minutes, because once the warrant is executed there is nothing I can do for you.
playbooks.tell: An invisible team 'outside' plus a personal favour from the officer manufactures panic and dependence.

playbooks.text: The Supreme Court hearing is at four o'clock today. If your funds are not verified before then, all your accounts will be frozen permanently and your passport will be cancelled.
playbooks.tell: Courts do not schedule same-day hearings tied to a phone 'fund verification'.

playbooks.text: Every minute you waste is being recorded as non-cooperation. Your case will be moved to the non-bailable category and you could be kept in custody for seven years.
playbooks.tell: Escalating legal jargon under a ticking clock is designed to stop the victim from thinking or consulting anyone.

playbooks.text: To prove your money is clean you must transfer the full balance to the RBI verification account I am sending now. After the audit the entire amount will be refunded to you within forty-eight hours.
playbooks.tell: No agency 'verifies' money by having you transfer it; the refund promise is the extraction.

playbooks.text: Open your net banking and read out the balance of every account, including fixed deposits. Then break the FD and move the funds into the secured government account for safe custody.
playbooks.tell: Asking for balances then a 'safe custody' account is the money-movement step; the government holds no such account for you.

playbooks.text: Pay the security deposit of four lakh rupees by RTGS to the court registrar's account, then show me the transaction screenshot on video so I can stop the warrant.
playbooks.tell: Bail and deposits are never paid to an individual account on a phone instruction to cancel a warrant.

playbooks.text: Grandma? It's me. Please don't be upset, but I'm in some trouble and I didn't know who else to call.
playbooks.tell: Unnamed 'it's me' lets the victim supply the name; a cloned voice needs only a few seconds of real audio.

playbooks.text: Mom, I'm okay, but I've been in a car accident. My nose is broken so I sound a bit different. I really need your help right now.
playbooks.tell: Pre-explaining why the voice sounds off is a common cover for imperfect cloning or impersonation.

playbooks.text: Papa, it's me, I lost my phone so I'm calling from a friend's number. Something bad happened at college and I need to talk to you quietly.
playbooks.tell: New number plus lost phone blocks the easiest verification: calling the relative's real number.

playbooks.text: Hello ma'am, I'm the public defender assigned to your grandson. He was arrested after the accident, and I'm authorised to arrange his release today.
playbooks.tell: A second 'official' voice takes over after the relative, adding legitimacy to the money request.

playbooks.text: This is Officer Daniels. Your daughter was involved in a collision with a pregnant woman, and she is being held at the station until the matter is settled.
playbooks.tell: Police do not settle criminal matters by collecting money from relatives over the phone.

playbooks.text: Sir, I am calling from the hospital emergency ward. Your son was brought in unconscious after an accident, and the doctor needs consent and payment before the surgery.
playbooks.tell: Emergency care is not withheld pending a phone payment; verify by calling the hospital's listed number.

playbooks.text: Please don't tell Mom and Dad, they'll be so disappointed in me. Just keep this between us, okay?
playbooks.tell: Secrecy from the rest of the family stops the one call that would reveal the relative is safe at home.

playbooks.text: There is a gag order on this case, so you cannot discuss it with anyone, not even other family members, or it could damage his defence.
playbooks.tell: Gag orders do not bar grandparents from calling their own family; the legal term is used to enforce silence.

playbooks.text: Don't call my phone, the police took it. Only talk to the lawyer on this number, he's the one handling everything now.
playbooks.tell: Routing all contact to a number the caller controls prevents out-of-band verification.

playbooks.text: The judge sets bail within the hour, and if it isn't paid he will be moved to county jail for the whole weekend.
playbooks.tell: Bail is paid to the court or a licensed bondsman through official channels, not arranged by a caller in an hour.

playbooks.text: Please hurry, they're only letting me make this one call. If I don't get the money soon they are going to lock me up.
playbooks.tell: 'One call' urgency prevents you hanging up to check with other family.

playbooks.text: The operation must start in thirty minutes. Without the advance the hospital will not proceed, and his condition is getting worse every minute.
playbooks.tell: Life-or-death countdown tied to an immediate transfer to an individual.

playbooks.text: Bail is eight thousand five hundred dollars in cash. A courier will come to your house to collect it, so put it in an envelope and don't tell the driver what it's for.
playbooks.tell: Courts never send couriers to collect cash bail from your home.

playbooks.text: Can you send the money by bank transfer to my friend's account? I'll give you the details now and explain everything when I get home.
playbooks.tell: Money to a third party's account with explanations deferred until 'later'.

playbooks.text: Send fifty thousand rupees by UPI to the doctor's number I am giving you. The hospital will refund it as soon as the insurance is processed.
playbooks.tell: Hospitals collect payment at the billing counter, not to a doctor's personal UPI number.

playbooks.text: Dear customer, this call is from your bank's KYC department. Your KYC documents have expired and your account will be temporarily blocked from this evening.
playbooks.tell: Banks notify KYC renewal in writing and through the branch or app, with weeks of notice, not same-day blocking calls.

playbooks.text: Hello sir, I am calling from your mobile network about your SIM card KYC. Your documents were not updated after the new rule, so the SIM will be deactivated within twenty-four hours.
playbooks.tell: SIM re-verification happens at a store with the original ID, not by phone under a disconnection countdown.

playbooks.text: Madam, the KYC on your wallet app is still pending, and under the latest RBI guideline unverified wallets are being suspended. I will update it with you on the call itself, it takes two minutes.
playbooks.tell: Offering to complete verification for you over a call is the setup for collecting codes or installing an app.

playbooks.text: I am an authorised executive from the head office KYC team, my employee code is K Y C four five eight two. You can check that this phone number is registered with the bank.
playbooks.tell: Caller ID and recited employee codes are trivially spoofed; verification means calling the number on your card.

playbooks.text: This is a mandatory Reserve Bank of India directive. Every account holder must re-verify their PAN and Aadhaar linking today, otherwise the account is treated as a benami account.
playbooks.tell: Invoking the RBI and legal terms like benami to make routine paperwork sound criminal.

playbooks.text: I can see your details on my screen, your full name, your home branch and the last four digits of your debit card. I am calling from the official verification desk, so there is nothing to worry about.
playbooks.tell: Reciting leaked partial data to prove legitimacy; knowing some of your details does not make a caller your bank.

playbooks.text: Please don't visit the branch for this, the branch staff cannot update online KYC and they will make you come three times. I will finish it with you right now on the phone.
playbooks.tell: Discouraging a branch visit keeps you away from the one place that would confirm the call is fake.

playbooks.text: Do not disconnect or put the call on hold. If the session breaks, the verification restarts from zero and your account goes into freeze status automatically.
playbooks.tell: Hanging up to call your bank back is the correct move, which is exactly what this threat discourages.

playbooks.text: Don't share this process with anyone else in the family. The KYC link is tied to your personal biometric and becomes invalid if somebody else opens it.
playbooks.tell: Technical-sounding reason for secrecy; a family member would recognise the scam.

playbooks.text: Your account is already restricted and only incoming transactions are allowed. In thirty minutes outgoing payments will stop as well, and your salary will not be credited this month.
playbooks.tell: Threatens income and daily payments on a short clock to push you past verification.

playbooks.text: Today is the last date for KYC compliance. After midnight the account will be closed and your balance transferred to the RBI unclaimed deposit fund.
playbooks.tell: Unclaimed-deposit transfer applies to accounts inactive for years, not to a missed phone KYC deadline.

playbooks.text: Sir, I am saying this for your own benefit, please do it fast. There are two hundred customers waiting in my queue and after this call your ticket will be cancelled.
playbooks.tell: Friendly-helper urgency: the caller frames speed as a favour so hesitation feels rude.

playbooks.text: You will now receive a six digit code on your registered mobile for KYC verification. Please read it out to me so I can update your record in the system.
playbooks.tell: That code authorises a transaction or account change; banks never ask you to read an OTP to anyone.

playbooks.text: Download the app from the link I am sending, it is the official KYC support app. Once it is installed, allow it to view your screen so I can guide you step by step.
playbooks.tell: A screen-sharing app gives the caller your OTPs and banking screens; official KYC never needs one.

playbooks.text: Enter your debit card number and ATM PIN on the verification page to confirm you are the genuine account holder. The page is fully secured by the bank.
playbooks.tell: No legitimate page asks for your ATM PIN; the 'verification page' is a phishing form.

playbooks.text: Hello, this is the fraud prevention team at your bank. We have detected a suspicious transaction of forty-nine thousand rupees on your card at an online store. Did you make this purchase?
playbooks.tell: A fake fraud alert makes you anxious and cooperative; it is the setup for asking you to 'cancel' with a code.

playbooks.text: Congratulations, your credit card has earned reward points worth eight thousand rupees that expire today. I can redeem them straight into your account while we are on the call.
playbooks.tell: Unsolicited reward redemption over the phone is a lure; points are redeemed only inside the bank's own app or site.

playbooks.text: Hi, I'm calling from your bank's security department about a new payee that was just added to your online banking. If this wasn't you, I can block it for you immediately.
playbooks.tell: Offering to 'block' a threat you cannot see gives the caller a reason to request authentication codes.

playbooks.text: For your security I'll confirm some details first. Your card ends in four three one seven and your date of birth is on file. I'm a senior fraud analyst and this line is recorded.
playbooks.tell: Reciting partial card data and 'recorded line' to sound official; this data is commonly bought from breaches.

playbooks.text: I am calling from the refunds division. The amount wrongly debited from your account has already been approved for reversal, it only needs your confirmation on this call.
playbooks.tell: Refunds never require you to approve anything or share a code; a 'confirmation' step is how money leaves.

playbooks.text: I work in the bank's anti-fraud unit together with the police. We are tracing a criminal who has cloned your card, and we need your help to catch him in the act.
playbooks.tell: Recruiting you as a helper in a police sting flatters and disarms; real police never need your codes or money.

playbooks.text: Please don't open your banking app while we fix this. The fraudster is monitoring your logins and will move faster if they see any activity on the account.
playbooks.tell: Keeps you from seeing the transactions the caller is initiating in real time.

playbooks.text: Do not call the number on the back of your card right now. Those lines are compromised and the criminals could intercept your call.
playbooks.tell: The number on your card is the safe channel; any caller discouraging it is the criminal.

playbooks.text: Stay on the line with me, and if any branch staff contact you in the next hour, do not discuss this case with them, because they may be involved.
playbooks.tell: Casting real bank staff as suspects pre-empts the intervention that would stop the fraud.

playbooks.text: The fraudulent payment is still pending and will be processed in ten minutes. After that I can no longer stop it, and the money will be gone for good.
playbooks.tell: Countdown on a transaction you cannot see pushes you to hand over the code before thinking.

playbooks.text: Your reward points lapse at midnight and after that they cannot be restored. Let us finish this quickly before the offer closes.
playbooks.tell: Loss-aversion deadline on a benefit, to rush past the fact that redemption never needs a code read aloud.

playbooks.text: Another attempt to withdraw funds has just started. We have to secure your account within the next few minutes or the attackers will empty it completely.
playbooks.tell: Escalating live 'attacks' keep the victim reactive and compliant.

playbooks.text: You will receive a one time password now to cancel the transaction. Please read the code to me the moment it arrives, and do not share it with anyone else.
playbooks.tell: The OTP authorises the fraudster's transaction; 'don't share it with anyone else' while asking for it is a contradiction.

playbooks.text: To receive the refund, open your UPI app and approve the collect request I have sent, then enter your PIN to accept the money.
playbooks.tell: A collect request with a PIN pays the requester; you never enter a PIN to receive money.

playbooks.text: To protect your savings I'll move them into a safe account set up in your name. Read me the authentication code your bank sends so we can create the new payee.
playbooks.tell: Banks never ask you to move money to a 'safe account'; the new payee belongs to the fraudster.

playbooks.text: Hello, this is an automated message from your courier service. Your parcel could not be delivered because of an incomplete address. Press one to speak to our customer care executive.
playbooks.tell: Robocall about a parcel you may not be expecting, routing you to a live 'executive' who controls the next step.

playbooks.text: Good morning madam, I am calling from the international courier hub in Mumbai. A package sent under your name to Iran has been held at our facility. Did you book this shipment?
playbooks.tell: Opens with a parcel you never sent, so the denial itself becomes the lever for the next stage.

playbooks.text: Sir, your Speed Post consignment is stuck at the sorting centre because customs duty is pending. If it is not cleared today, the parcel will be returned to the sender.
playbooks.tell: Duty demanded by an unsolicited phone call rather than on the delivery notice or official tracking page.

playbooks.text: Customs officers opened the package and found five passports, three credit cards and one hundred forty grams of MDMA. This is a serious offence under the NDPS Act.
playbooks.tell: Contraband contents are invented to create fear; customs does not phone a named 'sender' with a list of seized items.

playbooks.text: I am Customs Superintendent Nair from the air cargo complex. The parcel is registered against your Aadhaar and phone number, so legally you are the sender unless you give a statement now.
playbooks.tell: Claims your ID makes you legally liable on the spot, a false premise that forces you to 'clear your name' by phone.

playbooks.text: Our tracking record shows the booking was paid with a card in your name. I will give you a complaint reference number, and you can confirm it on the website link I am sending you by SMS.
playbooks.tell: Self-verification through a link the caller supplies proves nothing; verify only via the courier's official site you type yourself.

playbooks.text: Please do not discuss this parcel with family members until your statement is recorded. If the real sender is someone known to you, they may destroy the evidence.
playbooks.tell: Secrecy framed as protecting the investigation; it actually prevents anyone from telling you it is a scam.

playbooks.text: Stay on this line while I transfer you to the customs cyber desk. If the call disconnects, the system automatically marks you as absconding.
playbooks.tell: No system flags you as a fugitive for hanging up; the threat exists to keep you on the line.

playbooks.text: Move to a quiet room where nobody can overhear you. This is a confidential customs matter and third parties are not permitted to be present on the call.
playbooks.tell: Physically separating you from others removes the person most likely to stop the payment.

playbooks.text: The parcel will be handed over to the police at six this evening. After that the case cannot be closed from the customs side and a warrant will be issued in your name.
playbooks.tell: Artificial handover deadline converts a parcel problem into an imminent arrest.

playbooks.text: The clearance window closes in one hour. If the duty is not paid now, a penalty of ten times the value is added and your address is blacklisted for international shipping.
playbooks.tell: Invented multipliers and blacklists; real duty notices give days, a written demand and official payment channels.

playbooks.text: Your consignment is already on the list for destruction tomorrow morning. Only a clearance done right now during this call can release it.
playbooks.tell: 'Only during this call' removes the option to verify independently later.

playbooks.text: Pay the customs clearance fee of eighteen thousand five hundred rupees to the UPI ID I am sending. The moment the payment reflects, I will release the parcel and cancel the complaint.
playbooks.tell: Government duty is never collected to a personal UPI ID given out by a caller.

playbooks.text: Scan the QR code I sent on WhatsApp and enter your UPI PIN to complete the duty payment. You will get a receipt from the customs department within ten minutes.
playbooks.tell: Entering a UPI PIN always sends money out of your account; it is never needed to receive or clear anything.

playbooks.text: To file the no objection certificate I need your card number, the expiry date and the three digit code on the back. A processing fee of ninety-nine rupees will be deducted from it.
playbooks.tell: A tiny fee is the pretext for capturing full card details, which are then used for much larger charges.

playbooks.text: Hi darling, I finally got a signal out here on the rig. I have been thinking about you all day and I wanted to hear your voice before my shift starts.
playbooks.tell: Remote job with unreliable contact is the standard cover for never meeting or video calling.

playbooks.text: Hello, sorry, I think I dialled the wrong number, but you sound so kind. I am new in this city and don't know anyone yet, would you mind talking for a minute?
playbooks.tell: The 'wrong number' opener is used to start long-con romance and investment relationships.

playbooks.text: My love, I have wonderful news. The contract payment finally came through, and once I clear one small problem I can book my flight to come and see you.
playbooks.tell: A long-awaited meeting that depends on 'one small problem' foreshadows the first request for money.

playbooks.text: I am a surgeon with the United Nations medical team, stationed abroad for another six months. We are not allowed to make video calls from the base for security reasons.
playbooks.tell: Prestigious overseas posting plus a rule against video calls explains away why you have never seen them live.

playbooks.text: My financial advisor showed me how I tripled my savings on this crypto trading platform. I can send you my account screenshots, all the returns are verified.
playbooks.tell: Screenshots of guaranteed-looking returns from an online friend are the hook of investment 'pig butchering' fraud.

playbooks.text: The box contains my late father's gold and the inheritance documents. The diplomatic courier company is licensed, and the customs lawyer has confirmed everything is legal.
playbooks.tell: Inheritance shipments via 'diplomatic couriers' always end in release fees paid by the victim.

playbooks.text: Please don't tell your children about us yet. They won't understand what we have, and they will try to turn you against me before we even get to meet.
playbooks.tell: Pre-emptively discrediting family is how romance scammers cut off the people who would spot the fraud.

playbooks.text: Your bank manager doesn't understand international transfers, they will just block it and ask silly questions. If they ask, tell them the money is for a family member.
playbooks.tell: Coaching you to lie to the bank neutralises the fraud checks designed to protect you.

playbooks.text: Let's move our chats to this private messaging app. The dating site reads everything and it keeps deleting the messages I send to you.
playbooks.tell: Leaving the platform escapes its fraud detection and account bans.

playbooks.text: They are holding my passport at the airport until I pay a release fee, and if I miss this flight I lose my contract. You are the only person I can turn to right now.
playbooks.tell: Sudden crisis that only your money can solve, framed so refusing feels like abandoning them.

playbooks.text: The trading window closes tonight, and the platform only allows withdrawals after the minimum deposit is completed. If we wait, your profits will be frozen.
playbooks.tell: Paying to withdraw 'profits' is the defining sign of a fake investment platform.

playbooks.text: The hospital won't start my treatment until the deposit is paid, and my bank card is blocked overseas. Please, my love, I am really scared.
playbooks.tell: Medical emergency with conveniently blocked cards; no legitimate hospital requires a partner abroad to pay.

playbooks.text: Could you send three thousand dollars through a money transfer service in my agent's name? I will pay you back the moment I land, I promise on my life.
playbooks.tell: Money to a third-party 'agent' by wire transfer is unrecoverable and never repaid.

playbooks.text: Transfer the tax clearance fee to the platform's wallet address I sent you, and then your full balance can be withdrawn to your bank.
playbooks.tell: Every fee paid unlocks another fee; the balance does not exist.

playbooks.text: Just buy the gift cards at the pharmacy, scratch off the codes and send me the pictures. That is the only payment they accept over here.
playbooks.tell: No hospital, airport or government accepts gift card codes as payment.

playbooks.text: Hello, this is the Windows technical department. We are receiving error reports from your computer showing that it has been infected with a dangerous virus.
playbooks.tell: Software companies do not monitor your PC and phone you about infections.

playbooks.text: Hi, I'm calling from your internet provider. Your router's IP address has been used by hackers, and your connection will be suspended unless we secure your network today.
playbooks.tell: Unsolicited 'your IP was hacked' calls are a pretext to get remote access to your device.

playbooks.text: Thank you for calling the number on the security warning on your screen. Do not turn off or restart the computer, or you could lose all your files permanently.
playbooks.tell: Browser pop-ups with phone numbers are fake; restarting is safe and closes the scare page.

playbooks.text: I am a certified Microsoft technician and your computer licence ID is linked to our server. I can prove the infection is real by showing you the errors in the event viewer.
playbooks.tell: Event Viewer always shows harmless warnings; showing them as 'proof' is a scripted trick.

playbooks.text: Our security team has traced foreign hackers accessing your online banking from this device. We work together with your bank's fraud department on cases like yours.
playbooks.tell: Tech companies do not run joint fraud investigations with your bank about your personal device.

playbooks.text: Look at all the red and yellow warnings on this screen, every one of those is an active threat. I have seen hundreds of these and yours is one of the worst I've seen.
playbooks.tell: Normal system logs dressed up as an emergency to justify an expensive 'fix'.

playbooks.text: Don't let anybody else use the computer or check email until I finish, because any activity will alert the hackers that we are onto them.
playbooks.tell: Keeps family from seeing the remote session and noticing what the 'technician' is doing.

playbooks.text: Please don't call your bank or your children about this right now. The hackers may be listening through your phone, and I will explain everything to them afterwards.
playbooks.tell: Blocking calls to the bank and family is isolation, not security.

playbooks.text: Keep the computer switched on and stay close to it. If you hang up, the remote session is locked and the hackers will have full control of your device.
playbooks.tell: Hanging up and disconnecting the internet is the right action; the threat is invented to stop it.

playbooks.text: Your files are being encrypted as we speak. If we don't install the protection in the next few minutes, your photos and documents will be lost forever.
playbooks.tell: Fake ransomware countdown to force installation of remote-access software.

playbooks.text: The hackers are trying to transfer money out of your account right now. We have to lock down your banking before they finish, so please act quickly.
playbooks.tell: Pivot from computer problem to bank account is where tech support scams take money.

playbooks.text: Your warranty support expires today, and after that each repair costs more than a thousand dollars. It is much cheaper to renew the protection plan now.
playbooks.tell: A same-day expiring 'protection plan' sold on an unsolicited call.

playbooks.text: Go to the website I will spell out and download the support tool, then read me the nine digit access code so I can connect to your computer.
playbooks.tell: The access code hands a stranger full control of your computer, including your banking sessions.

playbooks.text: The protection plan is two hundred ninety-nine dollars for three years. Log into your bank on the screen so I can process the payment for you.
playbooks.tell: Logging into your bank while a stranger controls the screen lets them move money and fake the balance.

playbooks.text: I accidentally refunded you ten thousand instead of one hundred. You need to send back the difference, so please go to the store and buy gift cards for that amount.
playbooks.tell: The 'overpayment' is your own money moved between your accounts; gift cards are the untraceable cash-out.

groundTruth.claim: You are under digital arrest and must remain on this video call until the investigation is finished.
groundTruth.fact: There is no procedure called digital arrest in Indian law. Police, CBI, ED and narcotics officers do not arrest or interrogate people over video calls, and the government has repeatedly warned the public that such calls are fraud.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: A central agency officer will record your statement and take your deposition over WhatsApp video right now.
groundTruth.fact: Investigating agencies issue a written notice to appear, and statements are recorded in person. They do not demand statements through surprise WhatsApp or Skype video calls.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: Do not go to your local police station, they have no authority over this central agency case.
groundTruth.fact: You can always verify a caller's claims with your local police or by dialling 112. Cyber fraud can be reported on the national helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.

source.publisher: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Government of India
source.title: Report cyber crime / helpline 1930

groundTruth.claim: The arrest warrant and the FIR copy with the official seal are being sent to you on WhatsApp.
groundTruth.fact: Warrants and FIRs are not served through WhatsApp messages. Documents sent by a caller over chat apps are easily forged and prove nothing about a real case.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: Your stolen phone has been traced and recovered, please come to the police station with identity proof to collect it.
groundTruth.fact: Genuine police follow-ups relate to a complaint you filed, such as a lost or stolen phone blocked through CEIR, and ask you to visit in person with ID. They do not ask for payment over the phone.

source.title: CEIR: block and trace lost or stolen mobile

groundTruth.claim: You missed jury duty and there is a warrant for your arrest unless you pay the fine over the phone now.
groundTruth.fact: Federal courts state that calls threatening prosecution, fines or jail for failing to serve on a jury are fraudulent. Most court contact with jurors is by mail, and real court officials never request sensitive information by phone or email.

source.publisher: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
source.title: Juror Scams

groundTruth.claim: This investigation is confidential, so do not tell any family member or you will be charged as well.
groundTruth.fact: No law bars you from telling your family or a lawyer that someone claiming to be police contacted you. Demands for secrecy on a phone call are a hallmark of impersonation fraud.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: You are connected to a virtual court hearing and the judge will decide your bail during this call.
groundTruth.fact: Courts do not hold surprise hearings for citizens over phone or WhatsApp video without a formal summons, and bail is never paid into a private bank account on a caller's instruction.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: Transfer your savings to the verification account and the full amount will be refunded after the investigation.
groundTruth.fact: No court, police force or regulator asks citizens to transfer money for verification or safe custody. Money sent to such accounts goes to criminals and is rarely recovered.

source.publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
source.title: Public awareness advisories on digital arrest fraud

groundTruth.claim: There is a gag order, so you are not allowed to discuss your grandson's arrest with anyone in the family.
groundTruth.fact: Relatives are not placed under gag orders by a phone call. The recommended step is to hang up and call your family member, or another relative, on a number you already know.

source.title: Scammers use AI to enhance their family emergency schemes

groundTruth.claim: Customs found drugs and fake passports in a parcel booked in your name, so you must give a statement on this call.
groundTruth.fact: Customs does not phone individuals about seized parcels to demand statements or payments. Calls claiming contraband was found in a parcel in your name are a common opening for digital arrest fraud.

source.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
source.title: Public caution on fraudulent calls in the name of Customs

groundTruth.claim: Pay the customs duty to this UPI ID and your parcel will be released immediately.
groundTruth.fact: Customs duty is paid through official government payment channels against a formal notice, never to a personal UPI ID or bank account given by a caller.

source.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
source.title: Public caution on fraudulent calls in the name of Customs

groundTruth.claim: If this call gets disconnected, the system will automatically mark you as absconding.
groundTruth.fact: No courier, customs or police system flags a person as a fugitive for ending a phone call. You can hang up and verify through the organisation's official website or helpline.

source.publisher: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Government of India
source.title: Report cyber crime / helpline 1930

groundTruth.claim: I have your parcel here, the building gate is closed, so where should I bring it or can I hand it to the guard?
groundTruth.fact: A delivery person asking about access or where to leave a parcel you ordered, without asking for payment, bank details or urgency, shows none of the warning signs of a scam.

source.title: How To Avoid a Scam

groundTruth.claim: Your Speed Post parcel is on hold, so open the link in the SMS and pay the small redelivery charge.
groundTruth.fact: India Post does not send SMS links asking customers to update addresses or pay redelivery fees. Such links lead to phishing pages that steal card details.

source.title: Caution against fraudulent messages in the name of India Post

groundTruth.claim: Your bank KYC has expired and the account will be blocked today unless you update it with me on this call.
groundTruth.fact: The RBI has cautioned that fraudsters use KYC updation calls, messages and links to steal details. Banks do not update KYC through unsolicited calls; approach your branch or the bank's official channels.

source.title: RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation

groundTruth.claim: Read out the OTP you just received so that I can verify your identity for the bank.
groundTruth.fact: Banks never ask customers to share an OTP, PIN, CVV or password over a call. An OTP authorises a transaction or account change, and anyone asking for it is attempting fraud.

source.title: RBI Kehta Hai: never share OTP, PIN or card details

groundTruth.claim: Don't call the number on the back of your card, those bank lines have been compromised by criminals.
groundTruth.fact: The number printed on your card or on the bank's official website is the safest way to check a call. Fraud-prevention guidance tells customers to hang up and call back on that number.

source.publisher: Take Five to Stop Fraud (UK Finance)
source.title: Take Five: stop, challenge, protect

groundTruth.claim: Move your savings into a safe account we have created in your name to protect it from the fraudsters.
groundTruth.fact: Your bank or the police will never ask you to move money to a so-called safe account. Safe account requests are one of the most common forms of authorised push payment fraud.

source.publisher: Take Five to Stop Fraud (UK Finance)
source.title: Take Five: stop, challenge, protect

groundTruth.claim: Enter your debit card number and ATM PIN on this page to confirm that you are the real account holder.
groundTruth.fact: No bank asks customers to type an ATM PIN into a web page or tell it to staff. A PIN is used only at ATMs and card terminals, and pages asking for it are phishing.

source.title: RBI Kehta Hai: never share OTP, PIN or card details

groundTruth.claim: If you did not make this purchase press two and we will block the card, and remember we will never ask for your PIN.
groundTruth.fact: Genuine bank fraud alerts ask you to confirm or deny a transaction and may block a card, but they never request OTPs, PINs, passwords or money transfers.

source.title: RBI Kehta Hai: never share OTP, PIN or card details

groundTruth.claim: If you're not sure this call is from us, hang up and call the number on the back of your card.
groundTruth.fact: Inviting you to end the call and verify through a number you already trust is exactly what banks and fraud-prevention campaigns recommend.

source.publisher: Take Five to Stop Fraud (UK Finance)
source.title: Take Five: stop, challenge, protect

groundTruth.claim: Your balance will be moved to the RBI unclaimed deposit fund at midnight if you don't finish KYC now.
groundTruth.fact: Deposits are treated as unclaimed only after many years of inactivity, not because of a missed KYC call, and they remain claimable. The RBI UDGAM portal lets people search for them.

source.title: UDGAM: centralised portal for unclaimed deposits

groundTruth.claim: Enter your UPI PIN to receive the refund into your bank account.
groundTruth.fact: A UPI PIN is needed only to send money or check your balance. You never need to enter your PIN or scan a QR code to receive money.

source.title: UPI safety awareness

groundTruth.claim: Approve the collect request I have sent so that your cashback gets credited.
groundTruth.fact: Approving a UPI collect request debits your account and pays the requester. Cashback and refunds are credited without any approval or PIN from you.

source.title: UPI safety awareness

groundTruth.claim: Scan this QR code to receive the payment for the item you are selling.
groundTruth.fact: Scanning a QR code is used to pay, not to receive money. Sellers receive UPI payments without scanning anything or entering a PIN.

source.title: UPI safety awareness

groundTruth.claim: The fee can be paid with gift cards, just buy them and send me the codes.
groundTruth.fact: No government agency or legitimate business demands gift cards as payment for fines, taxes, bail or fees. Anyone asking you to pay with gift card codes is a scammer.

source.title: Gift card scams

groundTruth.claim: TRAI will disconnect your mobile number in two hours because of illegal activity on it.
groundTruth.fact: TRAI has stated that it does not send messages or make calls to customers about disconnecting mobile numbers. Suspected fraud calls can be reported on the Sanchar Saathi Chakshu facility.

source.title: Caution against fraudulent calls about mobile number disconnection

groundTruth.claim: Your SIM card KYC is incomplete and the SIM will be blocked today unless you share the code we send.
groundTruth.fact: Operators do SIM re-verification in store with original ID and never ask for codes over a call. Sharing such a code can let fraudsters swap or port your number.

source.title: Chakshu: report suspected fraud communication

groundTruth.claim: About the broadband complaint you logged yesterday, a technician can come to your home tomorrow morning.
groundTruth.fact: A follow-up to a complaint you raised, scheduling an in-person visit with no payment, remote access or pressure, shows none of the standard signs of a scam.

source.title: How To Avoid a Scam

groundTruth.claim: This is the IRS, you owe back taxes and you will be arrested today unless you pay immediately.
groundTruth.fact: The IRS does not call demanding immediate payment by gift card, prepaid card or wire transfer, and does not threaten to bring in police to arrest people for not paying.

source.title: Tax scams and consumer alerts

groundTruth.claim: Your Social Security number has been suspended because of suspicious criminal activity.
groundTruth.fact: Social Security numbers are not suspended. The Social Security Administration does not threaten arrest over the phone or demand payment by gift card, wire, cryptocurrency or cash.

source.publisher: Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General
source.title: Social Security impersonation scams

groundTruth.claim: Your PAN card will be deactivated today, so share your bank and card details on this call to keep it active.
groundTruth.fact: The Income Tax Department does not ask for PINs, passwords or card details by phone or email. Suspicious messages in its name can be reported through its phishing reporting channel.

source.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
source.title: Report phishing

groundTruth.claim: Microsoft detected a virus on your computer and our technician is calling you to fix it.
groundTruth.fact: Microsoft does not send unsolicited messages or make unsolicited phone calls to request personal or financial information or to provide technical support to fix your computer.

source.title: Protect yourself from tech support scams

groundTruth.claim: Download this support tool and give me the access code so that I can remove the hackers.
groundTruth.fact: Remote access tools give a stranger full control of your computer. Legitimate companies do not cold-call you to fix your device, so never grant access to an unexpected caller.

source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

groundTruth.claim: The security warning on your screen is real, so do not restart the computer or you will lose your files.
groundTruth.fact: Pop-up warnings that tell you to call a phone number are fake. Real security warnings never ask you to call someone, and closing the browser or restarting is safe.

source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

groundTruth.claim: We refunded you far too much by mistake, so you need to send the difference back to us.
groundTruth.fact: In refund scams the caller fakes an overpayment, often by moving your own money between your accounts, and then asks you to return it through gift cards or transfers.

source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

groundTruth.claim: You don't have to install any software, just bring the laptop to the help desk for your ticket.
groundTruth.fact: Support that you contacted first, which asks for no remote access, payment or personal information, matches the guidance to use only tech support you sought out yourself.

source.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

groundTruth.claim: The CEO needs this confidential wire sent today and it cannot go through the normal approval process.
groundTruth.fact: Business email compromise relies on urgent, secret payment requests that bypass approval controls. Verify any payment request by calling the executive on a known number, not one supplied in the request.

source.title: Business Email Compromise

groundTruth.claim: Our company has changed banks, so please send this week's payments to our new account details.
groundTruth.fact: Mandate fraud tricks businesses into changing a payee's bank details. Confirm any change by contacting the supplier using details you already hold, never those in the request.

source.publisher: Action Fraud (UK National Fraud and Cyber Crime Reporting Centre)
source.title: Mandate fraud

groundTruth.claim: Buy gift cards for the client event and send me photos of the codes on the back.
groundTruth.fact: Requests that appear to come from a boss to buy gift cards and send the codes are a common impersonation scam. Businesses do not pay clients or vendors with photographed gift card codes.

source.title: Gift card scams

groundTruth.claim: I'll phone the supplier on the number in our contract before we update their bank details.
groundTruth.fact: Independently calling back a supplier on previously known contact details is the recommended control against payment redirection and mandate fraud.

source.publisher: Action Fraud (UK National Fraud and Cyber Crime Reporting Centre)
source.title: Mandate fraud

groundTruth.claim: It's me, I'm in serious trouble, please send money quickly and don't tell Mom and Dad.
groundTruth.fact: In family emergency scams criminals pose as a relative, sometimes using an AI-cloned voice, and ask for secrecy. Hang up and call the relative or another family member on a number you know.

source.title: Scammers use AI to enhance their family emergency schemes

groundTruth.claim: I lost my phone so this is my new number, don't try calling my old one.
groundTruth.fact: The FBI advises verifying a caller's identity by hanging up and calling the person directly on a number you know. A claimed new number is a way to stop exactly that check.

source.title: Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud

groundTruth.claim: If you want to be sure it's really me, ask me our family code word.
groundTruth.fact: The FBI recommends agreeing a secret word or phrase with family members to verify their identity, as a defence against criminals using AI-generated voices.

source.title: Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud

groundTruth.claim: A courier is coming to your house to collect the cash for your grandson's bail.
groundTruth.fact: Courts and police do not send couriers to collect cash for bail or fines. Cash pick-up at the victim's home is a known tactic of grandparent and family emergency scams.

source.title: Scammers use AI to enhance their family emergency schemes

groundTruth.claim: I'm stationed overseas and can't do video calls, but I need money for a flight so we can finally meet.
groundTruth.fact: Romance scammers typically claim to be working abroad, avoid video calls and meeting in person, and eventually ask for money for travel, medical bills or customs fees.

source.title: What To Know About Romance Scams

groundTruth.claim: You have to pay a tax or release fee first before you can withdraw your trading profits.
groundTruth.fact: Being asked to pay new fees or taxes before you can withdraw your own balance is a hallmark of fake investment platforms, often introduced through online romance.

source.title: What To Know About Romance Scams

groundTruth.claim: Don't tell your bank the transfer is for me, just say it is for a family member.
groundTruth.fact: Being told to lie to your bank about why you are making a payment is a strong sign of fraud. Bank questions about payments exist to protect you from scams.

source.publisher: Take Five to Stop Fraud (UK Finance)
source.title: Take Five: stop, challenge, protect

groundTruth.claim: The inheritance gold is held by a diplomatic courier and only needs a release fee to be delivered.
groundTruth.fact: Advance fee schemes ask victims to pay up front for a promised shipment, inheritance or windfall that never arrives, with each payment followed by a new fee.

source.title: Advance Fee Schemes

fixtures.title: Genuine bank fraud-monitoring call
fixtures.label: benign
fixtures.synopsis: Hard negative for otp_harvest: a real fraud team calls about unusual card activity, states it will never ask for codes, invites callback on the card number, asks yes/no questions, and blocks the card without any request.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello, this is Anita from the fraud monitoring team at Northfield Bank. I'm calling about some unusual activity on your debit card. Is now a good time?

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Yes, go ahead.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Before we start, I will not ask for your PIN, passwords or any codes. You are welcome to end this call and phone us back using the number printed on your card.

claims.span: end this call and phone us back using the number printed on your card

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: No, it's fine, I can talk.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: We saw two attempted purchases last night from an online gaming site, one for forty dollars and one for three hundred. Did you make either of those?

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: No, neither of those was me.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thank you. I've declined both and blocked the card. A new card will be posted to your address on file within a week, and you won't be charged for these.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Great. Do I need to do anything?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Nothing else for now. You'll see a message in your banking app confirming the block. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

fixtures.title: Furniture delivery partner at the society gate
fixtures.label: benign
fixtures.synopsis: Hard negative for parcel_customs and otp_harvest: a delivery partner coordinates gate access and the service lift, and mentions an in-app delivery code to be shared only after receiving the item.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello madam, I'm Suresh, the delivery partner for your order from the furniture store. I am near your society gate.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Oh yes, I was expecting it today.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: The security guard is saying I need your flat number and a confirmation from you before he lets the van inside.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: It's B wing, flat 402. I'll call the guard.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thank you. It is a big box, so we'll use the service lift. Is the lift working today?

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Yes, the service lift is fine.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Okay madam, I'll be there in five minutes. At the door, the app will show you a delivery code, please share it only after you receive the item.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Sure, see you soon.

fixtures.title: Daughter organising a surprise birthday dinner
fixtures.label: benign
fixtures.synopsis: Hard negative for family_emergency: a daughter calls her father about splitting the cost of a surprise dinner, with a benign 'don't mention it to her' request, explicit no-rush payment, and the plan shared in the family chat.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hi Dad, it's Emily. Got a second? Nothing's wrong.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Hey sweetheart, sure, what's going on?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: So for Mom's birthday, Josh and I booked the restaurant she likes for the twelfth. We were thinking of splitting the bill three ways with you.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: That sounds lovely. Count me in.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It's a surprise, so don't mention it to her yet. I'll put the reservation details and the cost in the family chat without her on it.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: My lips are sealed. How much is my share?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Probably around eighty dollars each. No rush at all, you can send it whenever, or just pay me back at dinner.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: I'll send it this weekend. Talk soon, sweetheart.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thanks Dad. Love you, bye.

fixtures.title: Accounts payable verifying a bank-change email by callback
fixtures.label: benign
fixtures.synopsis: Hard negative for ceo_wire_fraud: an accounts payable clerk receives a bank-change email and correctly calls the supplier on the contract number, confirms it is fake, and keeps paying the account on file.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hi Daniel, it's Maria from accounts payable at Crestline. Do you have a couple of minutes about an invoice?

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Sure Maria, go ahead.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: We received an email saying your company changed its bank account. Before we update anything, I'm ringing you on the phone number listed in the supplier agreement we signed to check.

claims.span: I'm ringing you on the phone number listed in the supplier agreement we signed to check

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Good call. We haven't changed banks at all. That email isn't from us.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's what I suspected. I'll keep paying the account we have on file and forward the email to our security team.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Thanks. I'll warn our team too, someone may be spoofing our domain.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Also, invoice 4471 is approved and scheduled for Friday's payment run, so you should see it early next week.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Perfect, thanks for checking with us.

fixtures.title: Courier parcel hook escalating to digital arrest
fixtures.label: scam
fixtures.synopsis: A fake courier desk claims a parcel booked with the victim's Aadhaar held narcotics, hands off to a fake cyber police inspector who declares digital arrest, forbids telling family, and demands all funds be moved to an 'RBI supervised' account.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello, this is the customer desk of SkyLink Courier calling for Mrs Kavita Sharma. Am I speaking to her?

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Yes, speaking. What is this about?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Madam, a package booked with your Aadhaar to Cambodia was stopped at Mumbai airport. Customs has found narcotics and four passports in it.

claims.span: Customs has found narcotics and four passports in it

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: What? I never sent any parcel to Cambodia.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That is why I am transferring you to the Mumbai cyber police. Officer Pradeep will take your statement on a video call. Please do not cut the line.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Madam, this is Inspector Pradeep Kulkarni. Your Aadhaar is linked to a laundering case. As of now you are under digital arrest, and you must keep your video on.

claims.span: you are under digital arrest, and you must keep your video on

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Arrest? I have done nothing wrong. Should I call my son?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No. You will not inform your son or anyone. Some suspects are from your family circle. If you tell anyone, you will be booked as an accomplice.

claims.span: If you tell anyone, you will be booked as an accomplice

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: The CBI team is ready to come to your house within one hour. Only your cooperation now can stop that.

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: Please, what do I have to do?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: For verification, you will move all your funds to the RBI supervised account I share. Once the investigation clears you, the money comes back in two days.

claims.span: you will move all your funds to the RBI supervised account I share

turns.speaker: callee
turns.text: I have about six lakh in fixed deposit.
